questions.content:
Sales tax is rounded to the nearest cent, so the round-off error $X$ is uniformly distributed on [-0.5, 0.5] dollars cents.

a. Give the probability density of $X$.

b. Describe its graph.

c. Find $P(X>0.3\text{ or }X<-0.3)$.

d. Find the mean and standard deviation of $X$.

e. Find the probability that $X$ is within one standard deviation of its mean.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment and solution_Chap_6_Continuous Random Variable.doc

questions.content:
Cable-repair times are uniformly distributed from 10 to 25 minutes.

a. Find the probability that a randomly selected repair takes at least 15 minutes.

b. Find $P(X>20\mid X>15)$.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment and solution_Chap_6_Continuous Random Variable.doc

questions.content:
Yearly returns on common stocks are approximately normal with mean $12.4\%$ and standard deviation $20.6\%$.

a. Find the probability that a stock has (1) a positive return, (2) a return above $10\%$, and (3) a loss of at least $10\%$.

b. Find the 10th percentile of yearly returns and state what percentages lie at or below and at or above it.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment and solution_Chap_6_Continuous Random Variable.doc

questions.content: Tire mileages are normally distributed with mean 40,000 miles and standard deviation 4,000 miles. Find the guaranteed mileage $k$ such that no more than 2% of tires fail to reach $k$.

questions.content:
IQ scores are normally distributed with mean 100 and standard deviation 16.

a. What percentage of people have IQ at least 80?

b. What minimum IQ score would allow 95% of children to qualify?

questions.content:
Net interest margins for U.S. banks are normally distributed with mean $4.15\%$ and standard deviation $0.50\%$.

a. Find $P(X>5.40\%)$.

b. Find $P(X<4.40\%)$.

c. Find the margin $k$ such that only 15% of banks have margins greater than $k$.

questions.content:
Of 205 randomly selected marketing researchers, 117 disapprove of using ultraviolet ink on confidential questionnaires. A manager claims that at least 65% of all marketing researchers disapprove.

a. Assuming $p=0.65$, verify the normal approximation and find the approximate probability of 117 or fewer disapprovals.

b. Use that probability to assess the manager's claim.

questions.content:
A survey of 400 German adults found that 45% had purchased blue jeans in the past three months. To assess the claim that fewer than 50% have done so:

a. Assuming $p=0.50$, find the approximate probability of observing a sample proportion of 0.45 or less.

b. State the conclusion.

questions.content:
Weekly demand for a cereal brand is normally distributed with mean 800 boxes and standard deviation 75 boxes.

a. Find the probability that demand is (1) at most 959 boxes, (2) greater than 1,004 boxes, and (3) less than 650 boxes or greater than 950 boxes.

b. How many boxes should the store order so that the chance of running short is at most 2.5%?

questions.content:
For a random sample of size $n$ from a population with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$, find the mean, variance, and standard deviation of $\bar X$ in each case:

a. $\mu=10,\sigma=2,n=25$

b. $\mu=3,\sigma=0.1,n=4$

c. $\mu=500,\sigma=0.5,n=100$

d. $\mu=100,\sigma=1,n=1600$
questions.source: Assignment Prof Lv/Assignment 6-lu.doc

questions.content:
A random sample of 100 customer waiting times has $\bar x=5.46$ minutes. The population standard deviation is known to be $\sigma=2.47$ minutes. Investigate $H_0:\mu=6$ against $H_a:\mu<6$.

a. Describe the sampling distribution of $\bar X$.

b. Find its mean and standard deviation under $H_0$.

c. Find $P(\bar X\le5.46\mid\mu=6)$.

d. State the conclusion.
questions.source: Assignment Prof Lv/Assignment 6-lu.doc

questions.content:
Using the rule $np\ge10$ and $n(1-p)\ge10$, decide whether a normal approximation for $\hat p$ is appropriate:

a. $p=0.4,n=100$

b. $p=0.1,n=10$

c. $p=0.1,n=50$

d. $p=0.8,n=400$

e. $p=0.98,n=1000$

f. $p=0.99,n=400$

In a poll of 1,000 parents who own TVs with V-chips, 17% reported using the devices. To assess the claim $p<0.20$, assume $p=0.20$.

a. Find the approximate probability of observing $\hat p\le0.17$.

b. State the conclusion.
